transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2026-04-14
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Singh (Redwood AE), Carlos Ortega (Redwood SE), Ellen Park (SparkWorks Head of MLOps), Jordan Miles (CTO), Priya Desai (SRE Lead), Marcus Lee (Platform Engineer)

Summary: Quick kickoff to align onboarding steps, tenant mapping, staging vs prod network posture, data residency note, and initial sizing for Dedicated. Agreed to share runbook, infra diagram, and schedule a capacity workshop.

Topics: onboarding runbook, tenant mapping, VPC peering, staging benchmarks, SSO/SAML, SOC2 checklist, dedupe/caching, prefix/KV cache (spoken as KV cash at points), timeline for pilot

Action items (captured verbally in call): see metadata action_items and next_steps.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya S: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. uh I'm Maya from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account. We'll kick off quick, introduce and then Carlos will go into the technical intake.
[00:18] Jordan M: Yeah thanks, appreciate it. We got Priya, Ellen, Marcus on our side. Um Jordan here. We're trying to get the first pilot up in staging by mid-May so curious about lead times.
[00:32] Carlos O: Cool yeah, so from Redwood's perspective the typical onramp is runbook -> staging setup -> pilot -> prod cutover. For SparkWorks we want to map tenants and decide whether you want a single VPC with runtime tenancy or multiple VPCs per tenant.
[00:50] Ellen P: Quick question on that — we have strict data lineage for a couple of tenants, one is EU-only, so data residency matters. Can we put dedicated instances in eu-west and route only that tenant there?
[01:05] Carlos O: Absolutely. You can use region pinning. For Dedicated we can allocate a GPU pool in eu-west and route requests with a policy. There was a note in our docs about fallback behavior if that pool is saturated — it'll either queue or fallback to a lower-cost variant, depends on policy. (mumble: Redwood Dedicate -> Redwood Dedicated)
[01:29] Priya D: And for network, we want VPC peering not public egress — is that supported for staging? We prefer private link but want to keep the staging plane more locked down.
[01:42] Maya S: Yes, private deployments and VPC peering are supported. We'll share our peering checklist. For hosted staging we can do transit VPC or AWS PrivateLink depending on your infra.
[01:58] Marcus L: one practical ask: do you require hostnames to be resolvable on our side or do you provision endpoints in our VPC? in other words what do we change in DNS?
[02:12] Carlos O: We typically provision a NATed egress and a private endpoint inside the customer VPC for the control plane — oh sorry that sounded backwards — let me rephrase: control plane stays hosted, runtime can be in your VPC if you choose Private, or we create peered subnets for Dedicated. DNS will be normal internal hostnames, we'll provide the records.
[02:34] Ellen P: (overlap) When you say control plane hosted, is there any PII touching that plane? we are highly regulated.
[02:44] Maya S: Good callout. By default control plane metadata doesn't contain payload text. The platform can be configured so that payloads never leave your private network for Private deployments. We'll add the SOC2/ISO pack in the docs we send.
[03:02] Jordan M: timeline question — if we want a mid-May pilot, what's the critical path?
[03:12] Carlos O: Critical path is: (1) share network diagram and SAML metadata, (2) staging infra provisioning (we can do a 1-2 day sprint), (3) load sample prompts and run a short benchmark, (4) confirm SLA and canaries. If we start network and SSO this week we can target mid-May.
[03:33] Priya D: what's the typical time for a Dedicated pool to be provisioned?
[03:39] Carlos O: It depends on capacity and region — if it's a common region like us-west-2 it's often a few days. For eu-west it might be up to 10 business days if hardware needs scheduling. We'll run a sizing workshop to nail the numbers.
[03:58] Ellen P: On prompt and prompt-engineering — we have templated prompts and a reranking flow — do you support tool-calls / function calling hooks?
[04:12] Maya S: Yes we do. The platform supports streaming responses, function calling, and structured outputs. For reranking we also have an embeddings + rerank path that a lot of customers use. We'll need sample data to validate latency SLOs.
[04:31] Marcus L: Any guidance on tokenization variance and cost estimates? we want to understand both latency and per-token cost.
[04:40] Carlos O: We'll provide a cost worksheet — it shows token estimates, batching effects, and quantization tradeoffs. Note: batching reduces per-token cost but can increase tail latency; we'll run numbers based on your prompt length distribution.
[05:01] Jordan M: Can you explain prefix or KV cache? I heard some engineers call it KV cash earlier on a call I was on (laugh).
[05:09] Carlos O: (laugh) yeah KV cache — key-value cache. It's prefix caching for repeated context; it reduces compute for repeated prompts. We'll demonstrate in the benchmark.
[05:23] Ellen P: Security — SSO, RBAC, encryption at rest with KMS, HSM for keys — what are options?
[05:34] Maya S: SSO via SAML is standard, RBAC maps to teams and routes in the console. For Private deployments you can bring your own KMS/HSM or integrate our keywrap. We'll include the encryption and audit-log spec.
[05:50] Priya D: Audit logs — retention and format? we need to feed to our Splunk.
[05:56] Carlos O: We export structured audit logs; retention is configurable. We can push to your cloud logging with an HTTPS sink or S3 archival and you can ingest into Splunk. We'll include an example mapping.
[06:12] Jordan M: Any blockers around compliance questionnaires? we do an internal vendor questionnaire; will Redwood fill in typical security questionnaires?
[06:22] Maya S: Yes, we'll share our security packet and can fill vendor questionnaires for enterprise deals. For the pilot that's usually fine with the packet and ISO/SOC docs.
[06:35] Ellen P: For the pilot we want to measure both latency p50/p95 and cost per 1k tokens. Do you have a standard benchmark we run?
[06:45] Carlos O: We have a lightweight benchmark harness — we can run with your prompt set. It measures throughput, p50/p95, and token cost. We'll attach the harness link in the shared drive.
[07:02] Marcus L: How do we map tenants in the console? is it at API-key level or route level?
[07:10] Maya S: Tenancy can be mapped by token, route, or model alias. Common pattern: one API key per tenant and routing policy that pins certain keys to region/model. We'll show tenant mapping in the runbook.
[07:28] Jordan M: We have an internal pipeline that uses Kafka to fan-out requests — what's best practice for integrating?
[07:36] Carlos O: Typical approach is a small edge layer that translates Kafka messages to Redwood API calls with batching. We'll provide examples for continuous batching and backpressure handling.
[07:52] Priya D: If we use batching, how do we keep end-to-end latency low for interactive flows?
[07:59] Carlos O: Use mixed policies: micro-batching for interactive low-latency flows and larger batches for async workloads. Also prefix caching helps for repeated context. We'll recommend settings after seeing your QPS distribution.
[08:16] Ellen P: Regarding staging vs prod, what's recommended separation? separate VPCs, separate models, or different routing policies?
[08:26] Maya S: Best practice is separate runtime pools for staging and prod with isolated quotas and traffic shaping. You can use the same model versions but different rollout policies.
[08:41] Jordan M: Are there any gotchas around rollouts and canaries?
[08:46] Carlos O: Canary traffic routing is supported; you can route X% to new model versions and monitor quality/regressions. Our console has eval hooks to compare outputs on sample prompts.
[08:59] Marcus L: On data retention, we want logs for 90 days but ensure prompt text is not stored beyond 7 days except for the gold set. Is that feasible?
[09:10] Maya S: Yes that's configurable. We can set retention policies per-route and per-tenant. For Private you can have full control.
[09:20] Ellen P: Any notes on installing agents in our VPC for metrics? we want Prometheus metrics.
[09:27] Carlos O: We can push Prometheus metrics to your endpoint or you can scrapes our exporter in the peered subnet. Either works. We'll include a prometheus.yml snippet.
[09:42] Jordan M: Ok can we talk costs briefly — what levers do we have?
[09:49] Maya S: Unit costs: model choice, quantization, batching, KV caching, routing policies. We have Optimize recommendations that suggest quantization levels vs latency tradeoffs. For initial sizing we'll run a cost scenario sheet.
[10:05] Priya D: Any examples of customers with a similar multi-tenant setup?
[10:11] Maya S: We have anonymized case studies; we'll include a short reference of a SaaS customer with EU/US tenancy separation.
[10:20] (small cross-talk, note: transcription imperfect)
[10:30] Carlos O: Ok, proposed immediate next actions: Marcus, share infra diagram and SAML metadata; Ellen, share sample prompts and QPS targets; we will send runbook and security docs. Also schedule Dedicated sizing workshop week of Apr 27.
[10:48] Marcus L: Sounds good. I'll compile the network diagram and add notes on the firewall rules.
[10:54] Ellen P: I'll pull the sample prompt templates.
[11:00] Maya S: Great. Any other open questions?
[11:04] Jordan M: One small question: can we get an estimate of the cost delta between hosted and Dedicated for our expected QPS?
[11:12] Carlos O: We'll run the estimate in the sizing worksheet. Hosted is simpler but Dedicated gives predictability and lower unit cost at scale. We'll show both.
[11:23] Priya D: I want to flag monitoring alerts for increased latency — do you have out of the box alerting that maps to our incident channels?
[11:31] Carlos O: Yes, you can forward to PagerDuty or webhook, and create route-level alerts in the console. We'll include an example alert policy.
[11:45] Ellen P: Ok thank you, this is helpful.
[11:49] Maya S: Thanks everyone. We'll email the runbook, security pack, and the drive with the sizing worksheet today. Follow up: targeted workshop invite for Apr 27.
[11:59] (call winds down, participants drop)

Recap (verbal):
- Items to share: onboarding runbook, security pack (SOC2/ISO), staging network diagram, SAML metadata, sizing worksheet, benchmark harness link.
- Pilot target: mid-May, contingent on network and SSO completion.
- Workshop: Dedicated sizing week of Apr 27.

Links mentioned: onboarding runbook (https://redwood.example.com/runbooks/sparkworks-onboard), sizing worksheet (drive link), benchmark harness (https://github.com/redwood-inference/benchmarks), security pack (link to doc), network diagram placeholder (customer to share).

End of transcript.
